Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)
- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)
- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
</system-reminder>

content.text:
## Reviewed
PR #111 (`8ea090a0`..`pr-111-review`), 5 files. Tier check: all five sit under `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` — absent from both `frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, matched only by `squadA.md`'s `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**`. No Tier 1/2 path touched. Confirmed.

## Findings

**1. `<a>` is not in the parser's allow-list — the fallback message's link silently degrades to plain text.** `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx:28` — `ALLOWED_TAGS = ['p','ul','ol','li','strong','em','b','i']`. `'a'` is absent, so `parseRichText` takes the unwrap path (`:202`): tag dropped, text kept. Failure scenario: an EU merchandiser authors `environmentalMessage` with the link the Figma shows; it renders as inert, unstyled, unclickable body copy. Nothing warns — no console message, no visual cue, the tab looks fine. This PR is the first consumer to route site-pref copy (as opposed to BM `longDescription`, whose allow-list comment at `:21-24` scopes the list to "what Business Manager actually authors today") through this parser, so the assumption underpinning the allow-list is now out of date. **High confidence on the mechanism; the AC/Figma consequence depends on the link actually being in the signed-off design.**

**2. No test anywhere exercises the gate or the fallback chain.** `index.tsx:839-847`. Independently confirmed: `product-detail/` holds only `productInfo.test.ts`, `variantScopedPrice.test.ts`, `partials/staticProductHeader.test.tsx` — no `index.test.tsx`, no page-level `*.stories.tsx`, and `grep -rn environmental e2e` returns nothing. The mapper test only proves passthrough; the new story only proves the leaf renders a string. So the two-level `isBlankRichText` fallback and `=== true` gate — genuine branching logic, exactly `testing.md`'s "data mapping / complex state" category, and its explicit "a component with real logic gets its own test even when a hook/parent covers the rendered result" — has zero coverage. Failure scenario: someone reorders the ternary so `environmentalMessage` wins over AP21 notes, and every EU PDP silently shows boilerplate instead of the product's own copy. Nothing fails. **High confidence.**

**3. The `sx` reaches into `ZimmProductDescription`'s internals.** `environmentalQualitiesContent.tsx:24` — `'& > div > * + *'` targets the atom's own `chakra.div` wrapper (`zimmProductDescription/index.tsx:25`) to override its recipe's `'& > * + *'` rhythm (`zimmProductDescription.css.ts:78`). The specificity claim in the comment is correct (verified 0,1,1 vs 0,1,0), but the selector silently no-ops if that atom ever renders a fragment, adds a wrapper, or switches to `chakra.section`. `css.md` names this exact smell ("reaching into a child component's internals rather than styling its own root — a sign the styling belongs in that child"), and a 64px Figma design value applied from outside the recipe that owns block rhythm splits the canonical styling surface `overrideStyling.md` asks for. A recipe variant is the house-style fix. **Medium-high confidence — it works today, but the coupling is invisible from the atom's side.**

**4. Story title deviates from same-folder precedent and is the repo's only 3-level title.** `environmentalQualitiesContent.stories.tsx:12` — `'Pages/PDP/EnvironmentalQualitiesContent'`. All three siblings in `product-detail/partials/` use `Commerce/` (`Commerce/StaticProductHeader`, `Commerce/DetailsAndCareContent`, `Commerce/PdpFooterLinks`), as does the atom it wraps (`Commerce/ZimmProductDescription`). `Pages/` precedent exists (4 stories) but all are flat two-level, including the one other partial — `checkout/partials/payment.stories.tsx` → `Pages/CheckoutPayment`. `components.md` also says pages get one assembly story, "not a story per sub-section". Either `Commerce/EnvironmentalQualitiesContent` or flat `Pages/PdpEnvironmentalQualities` fits; `Pages/PDP/…` creates a one-off sidebar branch. **High confidence on the facts; cosmetic severity.**

**5. Nit — table alignment.** `productInfo.test.ts:59-62`: the three touched rows use a wider column than the surrounding 12, so the table now has two alignment gutters. Prettier doesn't format inside template literals, so nothing will fix it automatically. Cosmetic.

## Checked and correct (no action)
- **Type safety at the call site.** `envQualitiesContent` infers `string | undefined`; I verified with an isolated `tsc --strict` probe that `flag && val ? [{content: val}] : []` narrows to `string`, so `content: string` is sound.
- **Security.** No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in the chain. `attrs` is captured at `richText.tsx:151` but only ever tested for a trailing `/` (`:166`, `:203`) — never passed to `createElement`, so `href`/`target`/`onerror` cannot reach the DOM. Tag names come from Sets, not input. `richText.test.tsx:28-29` already covers `javascript:` and `data:` hrefs.
- **Graceful degradation.** `selectPdpProductInfo` returns `null` on `!product?.name`; every read is optional-chained; `=== true` means absent/undefined fields drop the tab rather than throw.
- **No orphaned trigger row.** `index.tsx:1274` derives `PdpFooterLinks`' `triggers` from `pdpDrawerTabs`, so the PDP link disappears with the tab on non-EU.
- Mapper fields use `type`, optional `?`, no `any`, no `!`; the leaf has JSDoc despite being single-page-exempt.
